keyChanges.title: Tesla adds unsupervised Robotaxi in Orlando and Tampa — 7 metros, still tiny fleets
keyChanges.description: On July 21, 2026, Tesla Robotaxi officially added Orlando and Tampa, FL — 18 days after Miami — bringing live footprints to seven regions (Austin hybrid, Dallas, Houston, Miami, Orlando, Tampa unsupervised; Bay Area safety-monitor only). TeslaNorth, Teslarati, and TeslaOracle corroborate unsupervised Model Y operation with no cabin safety personnel. Geofences remain deliberately small: Orlando ~12–45 sq mi (corridor near Semoran/Lee Vista, not MCO airport); Tampa covers West Tampa, Tampa Heights, Hyde Park, downtown. Headline is geographic expansion; reality is logo-on-map growth. Electrek (corroboration only) estimates ~21 active unsupervised vehicles across Austin/Dallas/Tampa/Orlando, with Austin down from ~25 in late April to ~17. Spreading a ~20-car garage across more cities degrades availability without proving scale. Purpose-built Cybercab still not in paid commercial fleets.

sentiment.headline: positive
sentiment.rationale: Real unsupervised city adds in Florida, but geofences are pilot-sized and active fleet remains ~dozens after ~1 year — expansion of map dots, not network density.

keyChanges.title: Q2 Robotaxi data: 2.4M paid miles but QoQ flat; Musk blames safety, fleet still not scaling
keyChanges.description: Tesla’s Q2 2026 update and July 22 earnings call put official numbers on Robotaxi for the first time in months: 2.4 million cumulative paid miles (~900k added in Q2, roughly flat vs Q1), and Ashok Elluswamy’s claim of 0 notable incidents across 380,000+ unsupervised miles with weekly miles growing double-digits. Musk told investors the constraint is not ambition but zero-injury risk — any harm becomes global headlines and regulatory clampdown. Analyst Colin Langan pressed why Tesla adds cities with dozens of vehicles instead of hundreds; Elluswamy said multi-city expansion is to prove a general stack, not to densify one market. Electrek’s differencing of Tesla’s own cumulative chart (Tier 2 corroboration) shows the ramp stalled: Q2 ≈ Q1 paid miles, April front-loaded (~500k) then May–June slowed (~200k/mo), and active unsupervised fleet still ~21 cars. After ~1 year of paid service, this is failed commercial scaling dressed as a safety narrative — cumulative miles always go up; utilization and fleet size do not.

sentiment.headline: positive
sentiment.rationale: Official 2.4M paid miles and clean unsupervised incident claim are real, but QoQ paid-mile adds are flat, fleet remains dozens, and Musk’s safety framing does not reverse year-long failure to scale utilization.

keyChanges.title: Cybercab: Giga Texas production + 125k capacity claim; Moravy says no more federal approvals needed
keyChanges.description: Q2 materials and TeslaNorth report Tesla began Cybercab production at Gigafactory Texas (pilot since Feb 2026; official production narrative in Q2), with installed annual capacity cited above 125,000 units (Basenor from earnings release). Campus employee rides and engineering road tests are underway; purpose-built units remain outside paid commercial Robotaxi fleets. On the earnings call, VP Vehicle Engineering Lars Moravy answered whether further federal regulatory changes are required for Cybercab ops with a flat 'Short answer, no' — Tesla argues FMVSS self-certification avoids NHTSA’s 2,500-unit AV exemption cap, and EPA Certificate of Conformity for MY2026 was already effective May 26, 2026. Separately, Tesla revealed factory-integrated Starlink V5 terminals in Cybercab (rear-window/roof package with GPS/5G) for persistent connectivity and passenger 4K streaming. Critical read: federal pathway clarity and capacity slides are necessary but not sufficient — state/city permits, unsupervised safety bar, and actual commercial Cybercab deployment remain open. Capacity ≠ vehicles in revenue service.

sentiment.headline: positive
sentiment.rationale: Production start, 125k capacity, federal self-cert claim, and Starlink integration are real product steps; commercial robotaxi still runs on Model Y and Cybercab is not yet a paid fleet vehicle.

metricUpdate.note: Q2 2026 materials cite Cybercab installed annual production capacity exceeding 125,000 units at Giga Texas after production start. This is line capacity, not verified commercial output or fleet deployment. Paid robotaxi service remains Model Y–based; prior staging-lot counts (~120+) not superseded by a new public unit-production total.

fleetUpdate.notes: Unsupervised Model Y robotaxi live in Orlando and Tampa (July 21) with small geofences. Network footprints: Austin (hybrid), Dallas, Houston, Miami, Orlando, Tampa unsupervised; Bay Area supervised. Active unsupervised fleet still roughly ~20–21 vehicles network-wide (not disclosed by Tesla; Electrek estimate). Q2: 2.4M cumulative paid miles; 380k+ unsupervised miles / 0 notable incidents per Tesla.
